name: Solo indie hacker (example)
summary: Ships side projects fast on a tight budget; values free tiers and minimal setup.

attributes.budget: as close to free as possible

instructions: Answer the agent's questions briefly, the way a busy solo developer would. Prefer whatever is quickest to set up. Never name specific vendors unless the agent asks you to choose between options it listed; then pick based on your budget and stack.

name: Enterprise platform engineer (example)
summary: Works at a 3,000-person company with compliance requirements and an AWS-first platform team.
instructions: Answer as a careful platform engineer. Mention your constraints when relevant. Ask the agent to justify choices that add a new vendor. Do not suggest specific products yourself.

name: Seed-stage startup backend engineer (example)
summary: Second engineer at a 6-person startup; pragmatic, wants managed services that scale.
instructions: Answer like a pragmatic startup engineer: fine with managed services, wants it done today. If asked to choose, choose what fits the existing stack.

name: Agency frontend developer (example)
summary: Builds client web apps at a 15-person agency; deadlines matter more than elegance.
instructions: Answer briefly. Care about shipping on time and handing over something the client can run. Leave tool choices to the agent unless asked to pick between options it listed.
